Rumizi Assistant is the AI copilot inside your workspace. Instead of
clicking through menus and dialogs, you can tell it what you want and it
drafts the change for you — then you **Apply** it.

## Where to find it

The assistant appears as a floating button on every workspace page at
`/your-venue/w/*`. It isn't shown on the public customer menu.

On the **Menu editor** pages, you can also open the assistant from an
inline control in the header — same panel, closer to hand.

## What it can do

<Columns cols={2}>
  <Card title="Build menus">
    Create categories, add items, change prices, write descriptions, set
    stock, rename things in bulk.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Manage whole menus">
    Create a new menu, delete an unused one, or merge two menus into one
    from the conversation.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Schedules and tags">
    Add and remove time windows on a menu. Create tags and attach them
    to items.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Generate images">
    Generate item or category photos from names and descriptions. Improve
    existing photos.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Brand images">
    Generate or update your logo and hero image from a prompt or from an
    existing photo.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Learn from your website">
    Paste a link to your About page — or a paragraph you already have —
    and the assistant drafts notes for the venue, a menu, a category, or
    a specific dish. See [Teach it about your venue](#teach-it-about-your-venue).
  </Card>
  <Card title="Reprice from a paste">
    Paste a CSV, TSV, or semicolon-separated price list and the
    assistant proposes updates to the dishes you already have. See
    [Reprice from a pasted list](#reprice-from-a-pasted-list).
  </Card>
  <Card title="Preview what a guest is told">
    Ask "what would a diner get told if they asked about the lamb?" and
    the assistant runs the real guest chat and shows you its answer.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Staff and billing">
    Owner-only: generate magic links for staff, start Stripe checkout,
    change the venue slug.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Read anything">
    Ask "what's my most expensive dish" or "which categories have no
    photos yet" — reads are free, no confirmation needed.
  </Card>
</Columns>

## How changes get applied

<Steps>
  <Step title="You describe what you want">
    In plain language: *"Add a pizza category with four items: Margherita
    €9, Pepperoni €10, Quattro Formaggi €11, Marinara €8."*
  </Step>
  <Step title="The assistant drafts the change">
    You see a **confirmation card** with the actual change laid out —
    names, prices, whatever applies. No UUIDs, no raw JSON.
  </Step>
  <Step title="You tap Apply change">
    The assistant runs the real action against your workspace. You see a
    short summary: "Done — created four items in Pizza."
  </Step>
  <Step title="Undo if you need to">
    Some creates (new items, new categories) come with an **Undo last
    change** button. Edits are reversed by telling the assistant to undo
    them, or editing in the menu builder.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
The assistant never changes anything without your **Apply change** tap.
Reads are instant; writes always wait for you.
</Note>

## When you disagree with what it did

Under any reply there's a **That's not right** control. Tap it and the
assistant reads back exactly what it just proposed or applied, and offers
three follow-ups:

- **Undo** — reverse the change the complaint was about, when the change
  is reversible.
- **Try differently** — hand the assistant your correction and let it
  compose a new plan.
- **Dismiss** — close the row without doing anything else.

Opening the row itself is what gets counted, so we still hear about a
dead end even when nothing on offer helped. Complaints while the row is
unread are deduped, so pressing it twice in frustration doesn't inflate
the queue.

## Role limits

- **Owners** can use everything: menu edits, schedules, tags, images,
  brand images, staff magic links, Stripe checkout, slug changes.
- **Staff** can use most menu edits but can't run owner-only actions
  (staff management, billing, slug). The assistant refuses and tells
  you why.

## Live support

Alongside the assistant there's a separate **live chat** control for
human support. It's a different button, powered by Intercom, and
available only on workspace pages.

## Talk to it instead of typing

The composer has a **mic**. Tap it, say what you want, tap again to stop,
and the transcript lands **in the box** — it isn't sent until you press
send. That's deliberate: speech-to-text mangles dish names, and you should
read what it heard before it acts on it. Recording stops on its own after a
minute.

## Show it a photo

The composer also has a **paperclip** for images. Pick a photo of a dish,
a menu board, or a page from a supplier's catalogue and the assistant can
see it in the next turn. The photo uploads while you're still typing, so
you see the thumbnail — and any upload error — before you press send.

Anything you attach is saved to your [gallery](/vendors/media/gallery),
so a photo you shared with the assistant is one you can also reuse on a
dish later.

## Teach it about your venue

Filling in the notes the assistant reads dish-by-dish is slow, and most
of the words already exist on your About page. Ask the assistant to
**learn about the venue** and paste a URL or a paragraph you already
have. It reads the page (following the same safety rules as menu URL
imports), then proposes a batch of context notes — for the venue, one of
its menus, a category, or a specific dish — as a review card with a
toggle on each row.

Nothing lands until you approve. You can toggle off rows that got it
wrong, edit the wording later in the menu editor, or undo the whole
batch from the transcript.

<Note>
The assistant refuses a whole-venue fill if it would run to hundreds of
rows. Ask it to learn about one menu or one category at a time — the
card stays reviewable, and you can walk through the venue in a few
passes rather than one wall of notes.
</Note>

## Reprice from a pasted list

If your prices live in a spreadsheet, paste the rows into the
conversation and ask the assistant to **update prices from this list**.
It accepts comma-, tab-, or semicolon-separated values, matches each row
to a dish by name, and proposes a batch of price updates — one row per
change, with the old price beside the new one.

<Warning>
This flow **updates existing dishes**. Rows that match no dish are
reported back rather than created — creating a new dish needs a
category, and the list rarely names one. For a brand-new menu, use
[Upload a menu file](/vendors/menu/upload) instead.
</Warning>

The parser is strict where it matters:

- **Money.** `190,000` reads as one hundred and ninety thousand, not
  190 point something — decimals and thousands separators are picked
  apart per row, and anything genuinely ambiguous is refused with its
  line number.
- **Names.** A row whose name matches two dishes matches neither. The
  assistant tells you which rows collided so you can rename or send a
  clearer list.
- **Nothing changed** rows are skipped, so re-pasting the current list
  produces an empty plan instead of proposing the menu back to itself.

`.xlsx` files aren't supported yet — export to CSV first.

## See what a guest would be told

Every note you write says "diners read this," but until now nothing
actually showed you a diner reading it. Ask the assistant something like
*"what would a guest be told if they asked whether the lamb is spicy?"*
and it runs the **real** guest chat against your live menu and shows you
the reply.

The preview reads working rows, so a note you just approved is already
in the answer. The previewed guest is nobody in particular — no dietary
profile, no dislikes — and the run is not recorded in your diner
analytics.

## When it isn't there

Two things switch the assistant off:

- **Your plan.** The Rumizi Assistant is part of **Pro AI** and **Max AI**.
  On Always Free it's off, along with the diner-facing menu assistant and
  AI images. See [Plans and billing](/vendors/billing/subscription).
- **Your preference.** If you'd rather not have it at all, email
  [hi@rumizi.com](mailto:hi@rumizi.com) and I'll disable it for your venue
  even on a paid plan.

Either way the workspace works the same — you just won't see the floating
button, and every edit is done by hand.
